items.title: SpaceX Crew-12 cleared to launch to ISS on Friday morning

featured_image.name: Crew-12 Targets Friday Launch as Expedition 74 Keeps Up Tech ...

items.description:
Four astronauts are set to blast off to the International Space Station early Friday morning, ending a monthlong period in which the orbiting laboratory operated with a skeleton crew following the first medical evacuation in NASA's history.

NASA and SpaceX received a "go" to proceed with the Crew-12 launch countdown on Thursday, targeting liftoff at 5:15 a.m. EST on February 13 from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Weather forecasters issued an improved outlook with a 90% chance of acceptable conditions at launch time.[1][2][3]

items.title: China completes first at-sea rocket booster recovery

featured_image.name: Long March-10's first stage retrieved from sea in China's first

items.description:
China successfully conducted a dual flight test of its next-generation Long March-10 carrier rocket and Mengzhou crewed spacecraft on February 11, marking what the China Manned Space Agency called "major breakthroughs" in the country's ambitious plan to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030.[1][2]

The test at the Wenchang Space Launch Site in Hainan Province achieved several firsts for China's space program, including the nation's first maximum dynamic pressure abort test of a crewed spacecraft and the first at-sea recovery of both a rocket booster and a spacecraft return capsule.[3][4]

items.title: Norway charges ex-PM Jagland with corruption over Epstein ties

featured_image.name: Ex-Leader of Norway Charged With Corruption Linked to ...

items.description:
Former Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjørn Jagland was formally charged with gross corruption on Thursday, February 12, as investigators probe his ties to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Norwegian police searched three of Jagland's properties and seized evidence after the Council of Europe lifted his diplomatic immunity just one day earlier.[1][2][3]

Økokrim, Norway's economic crimes unit, confirmed that Jagland now faces charges of gross corruption—a serious category under Norwegian law—following allegations that he accepted benefits from Epstein between 2011 and 2018. The 75-year-old denies any criminal liability and has pledged to cooperate with the investigation, according to his lawyer Anders Brosveet.[4][2][5][1]

items.title: Bangladesh's BNP wins two-thirds majority in first post-uprising election

featured_image.name: Once-Exiled Political Scion Set to Lead Bangladesh After BNP ...

items.description:
The Bangladesh Nationalist Party has declared victory in the country's first parliamentary election since a Gen Z-led uprising ousted longtime ruler Sheikh Hasina in 2024, positioning party leader Tarique Rahman to become the next prime minister after 17 years in exile.

The BNP and its coalition partners secured approximately 212 of 299 contested seats, surpassing the two-thirds majority threshold, according to local television reports and preliminary Election Commission data. The Islamist party Jamaat-e-Islami and its allies captured around 70 seats, with party leader Shafiqur Rahman conceding defeat and pledging to pursue "constructive politics" rather than obstructionist opposition.[1][2][3]

items.title: DeepMind VP says decoding human genome is AI's next frontier

featured_image.name: Pushmeet Kohli, Vice President of Research, Google DeepMind ...

items.description:
Artificial intelligence could help decode the "recipe book of life" hidden inside human DNA and transform India into a global hub for cutting-edge scientific research, according to Google DeepMind's Vice President of Research Pushmeet Kohli.

In an interview with Moneycontrol, Kohli said AI's biggest potential lies in the democratization of science, allowing researchers with modest resources to compete with the world's best-funded laboratories. He pointed to AlphaFold, the Nobel Prize-winning protein structure prediction model developed by his teams, as proof of that transformative power. "All of that millions of dollars and multiple years has been transformed into one click," Kohli said, referring to how AlphaFold has reduced work that once took years to complete to mere seconds.[1][2]

items.title: Space-based solar power gains global momentum amid grid demands

featured_image.name: china to build solar power stations in space

items.description: New developments in space-based solar power and radioisotope energy systems are drawing fresh attention from governments, investors, and industry leaders who say these technologies could fundamentally transform how the world generates electricity. The renewed push comes as energy demand surges and countries race to develop clean, reliable power sources that operate independently of weather and daylight constraints.

items.title: Deep Space Energy raises funds for lunar power technology

featured_image.name: Latvian startups conquer the space technology field ...

items.description:
From solar-powered orbital data centers to compact radioisotope generators, a wave of space-based power technologies is gaining momentum as governments and private companies race to harness energy beyond Earth's atmosphere.

SpaceX filed with the Federal Communications Commission in late January for approval to launch up to one million satellites that would function as orbital data centers, powered entirely by solar energy. The proposal represents the largest satellite constellation ever proposed and reflects growing interest in space as a solution to the surging energy demands of artificial intelligence computing. "By directly harnessing near-constant solar power with little operating or maintenance cost, these satellites will achieve transformative cost and energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centers," the company stated in its FCC filing.[1][2]

items.title: Iran fortifies nuclear sites amid US military buildup, images show

featured_image.name: Satellite photos show activity at Iran nuclear sites as tensions rise ...

items.description:
Iran is reinforcing defenses at its key nuclear facilities as new satellite imagery reveals expanded fortifications and tunnel construction, with activity intensifying as diplomatic efforts with the United States continue alongside growing military pressure.

Fresh images analyzed by the Institute for Science and International Security show tunnel entrances at the Isfahan nuclear complex being buried under soil, while construction activity continues at an underground facility near Natanz known as "Pickaxe Mountain," the BBC reported Wednesday. The developments come as President Donald Trump weighs deploying a second aircraft carrier to the Middle East and warns of "something very tough" if Iran fails to meet U.S. demands.[1][2]

items.title: Trump repeals EPA climate finding as UN chief warns of 'new world disorder'

featured_image.name: Trump revokes EPA finding on greenhouse gas threat in huge blow to climate change regulations

items.description:
The head of the United Nations climate body on Thursday urged countries to unite against what he called an "unprecedented threat" to international cooperation from pro-fossil fuel forces, delivering his stark assessment as the Trump administration took sweeping action to dismantle U.S. climate regulations.

Simon Stiell, Executive Secretary of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, addressed media in Istanbul alongside Turkey's incoming COP31 President Murat Kurum. The remarks came hours before President Donald Trump announced the repeal of a foundational scientific finding that underpinned federal authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions.

items.title: Europe's most powerful rocket launches Amazon satellites in maiden flight

featured_image.name: Inaugural Ariane 64 launches Amazon Leo satellites from ...

items.description:
Europe's most powerful rocket successfully reached orbit for the first time on Wednesday, carrying 32 satellites for Amazon.com, Inc.'s Leo broadband internet constellation in a launch that marks a new chapter for the continent's space ambitions.

The Ariane 64 lifted off at 16:45 UTC from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, deploying its payload to low-Earth orbit in a mission lasting one hour and 54 minutes. The successful debut flight confirms Europe's heavy-lift launch capability and represents the first commercial customer mission for the Ariane 6 rocket family.[1][2][3]

items.title: Anthropic closes $30B round, valuing AI firm at $380B

featured_image.name: Anthropic closes latest funding round above $10 billion and could go higher, sources say

items.description:
Anthropic announced Thursday that it has completed a $30 billion Series G funding round, valuing the San Francisco-based AI company at $380 billion post-money. The deal stands as the second-largest private technology fundraise in history, trailing only OpenAI's $40 billion round led by SoftBank in March 2025.[1][2]

Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC and Coatue Management led the financing, with co-lead investments from D.E. Shaw, Dragoneer Investment Group, Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, ICONIQ, and Abu Dhabi's MGX, according to a GIC press release and Bloomberg reporting. Strategic investors Microsoft and Nvidia, which committed up to a combined $15 billion in Anthropic last November, participated alongside Blackstone, Sequoia Capital, and Altimeter Capital.[3][4][5][6][2]

items.title: NASA tests repaired Artemis II rocket after hydrogen leak

featured_image.name: Rocket fuel leak delays NASA's Artemis II mission to the ...

items.description: NASA is loading liquid hydrogen into its Space Launch System rocket at Kennedy Space Center on Thursday in a previously unannounced test to verify seal repairs following a leak that halted a critical countdown rehearsal earlier this month. The test marks the latest milestone as the agency works toward launching Artemis II, the first crewed mission to the Moon since the Apollo era.

items.title: Astronomers find 'inside out' solar system with rocky outer planet

featured_image.name: Unique 'inside out' planetary system reveals rocky outer world

items.description:
An international team of astronomers has discovered a planetary system that challenges long-held theories about how planets form, with a rocky world orbiting farther from its star than two gas-rich planets. The discovery, published Wednesday in the journal Science, reveals the first evidence of a planet that may have formed in a gas-depleted environment.[1][2][3]

The system orbits LHS 1903, a red dwarf star located 116 light-years from Earth. Using the European Space Agency's CHEOPS satellite, researchers led by Dr. Thomas Wilson of the University of Warwick detected a fourth planet at the system's outer edge—one that unexpectedly appears to be rocky rather than gaseous.[2][4]

items.title: European stocks reverse from record highs as AI fears grip markets

featured_image.name: Stock Market Today: Major Indexes Plunge on Tech Stock Sell-Off; Dow Sheds 550 Points; AppLovin, Cisco Dive After Earnings

items.description:
European stock markets climbed to fresh all-time highs on Thursday morning as investors cheered positive corporate earnings from luxury and industrial companies, but gains faded later in the session as renewed fears about artificial intelligence disruption dragged global equities lower.

The pan-European STOXX 600 surged 0.7% to 625.86 points in early trading, setting a new record, according to Reuters. France's CAC 40 led regional benchmarks with a 1.4% rise. However, the rally reversed by the close, with the STOXX 600 ending down 0.5% as U.S. markets tumbled, Bloomberg reported.[1][2][3]

items.title: Russia dismisses Ukraine claim it can't run Zaporizhzhia plant

featured_image.name: Risks of disaster at nuclear plant ‘increasing every day’: Mayor

items.description:
Ukraine's state nuclear company has warned that a restart of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant under Russian control risks a nuclear accident, prompting a sharp rebuke from Moscow's atomic agency, which dismissed the allegations as unfounded.

Pavlo Kovtoniuk, acting chairman of Energoatom, told Reuters on Tuesday that Russia lacks the necessary equipment and spare parts to safely operate Europe's largest nuclear facility. "Russia will not be able to restart the station. The main equipment and the control, protection, and monitoring systems are all Ukrainian," Kovtoniuk said. "Without spare parts and without the project, the station simply cannot be operated."[1]

items.title: Iran reinforces key nuclear site as US diplomacy continues

featured_image.name: Satellite images reveal hidden activity at Iran's nuclear ...

items.description:
Fresh satellite imagery reveals Iran is hardening defenses at an underground tunnel complex near Natanz, its most critical remaining nuclear facility, as diplomatic negotiations with the United States continue and military tensions in the region escalate.

Images captured on February 10 by the Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS) show concrete being poured at tunnel entrances and heavy construction equipment actively reinforcing the site at Kolang-Gaz La Mountain, widely known as Pickaxe Mountain, located roughly two kilometers south of the Natanz enrichment facility.[1][2]

The fortification efforts come eight months after U.S. and Israeli airstrikes struck multiple Iranian nuclear sites during the June 2025 conflict. The United States conducted Operation Midnight Hammer on June 22, 2025, targeting the Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan nuclear facilities with bunker-buster bombs and Tomahawk cruise missiles. Pickaxe Mountain was notably not among the facilities targeted, though analysts say Iran has since accelerated construction there as its most important undamaged nuclear asset.[3][2][4][5]

items.title: Europe overtakes US as Ukraine's largest military backer, study finds

featured_image.name: Inside Europe's drive to get ammunition to Ukraine as Russia ...

items.description:
Europe has overtaken the United States as Ukraine's largest military backer for the first time since June 2022, according to new data from the Kiel Institute for the World Economy, marking a seismic shift in Western support as the war enters its fifth year.

The German think tank's Ukraine Support Tracker, published on February 11, shows that European nations have now provided €72 billion in total military aid to Kyiv, compared with €65 billion from Washington. The reversal follows a near-total collapse in American support under the Trump administration, with U.S. military aid plummeting 99% in 2025.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Russian memo floats return to dollar system in pitch to Trump

featured_image.name: The U.S.-Russia Plan Gives Trump a $300 Billion Signing Bonus

items.description:
The Kremlin has drafted an internal memo outlining proposals for sweeping economic cooperation with the United States that includes a return to the dollar system, according to market sources, as Moscow seeks to capitalize on the Trump administration's transactional approach to foreign policy.[1]

The high-level document, drafted this year, identifies seven areas where Russian and American economic interests could align, including cooperation on fossil fuels, joint investments in natural gas and offshore Arctic oil extraction, and opportunities for American companies in critical raw materials. The proposals are contingent on a deal to end Russia's war in Ukraine.[2][1]

items.title: Global stocks hit record highs on strong US jobs data

featured_image.name: KOSPI jumps over 3 pct to end at fresh high of above 5,500 ...

items.description:
Stock markets across Europe and Asia climbed to record highs on Thursday, buoyed by a stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report and upbeat corporate earnings that lifted investor sentiment.

The pan-European STOXX 600 reached an all-time high of 625.86 points, rising 0.7%, with France's CAC 40 leading regional benchmarks with gains exceeding 1.4%, according to Reuters. The rally was driven by strong quarterly results from French firms Legrand and Hermès, with Legrand reporting a 9.6% increase in annual revenue to 9.48 billion euros and adjusted operating profit up 10.5%.[1][2]

items.title: U.S. covertly sent 6,000 Starlink terminals into Iran, officials say

featured_image.name: Iran police seize 108 Starlink satellite devices amid ...

items.description:
The Trump administration covertly delivered approximately 6,000 Starlink satellite internet terminals into Iran after the regime's violent crackdown on nationwide protests last month, marking the first time the U.S. government has directly sent the technology into the country, according to U.S. officials cited by The Wall Street Journal.[1]

The operation was designed to help Iranian dissidents maintain communications after Tehran severely restricted internet access amid the deadliest wave of unrest in decades.
